apps.name: 1Password
apps.notes: 1Password has an official Linux app. Your vault syncs as usual.

apps.name: LastPass

alternatives.name: Bitwarden
alternatives.note: Imports LastPass exports.

apps.notes: LastPass has no Linux desktop app. Use the browser extension or move to Bitwarden.

apps.name: Dropbox
apps.notes: Dropbox has an official Linux client.

apps.name: Google Drive

alternatives.name: rclone
alternatives.note: Command-line tool that mounts Google Drive.

alternatives.name: Google Drive in a browser
alternatives.note: Files stay available in the web app.

apps.notes: Google's desktop sync app has no Linux version. Use Drive in a browser or rclone to sync.

apps.name: OneDrive

alternatives.name: OneDrive Linux client (abraunegg)
alternatives.note: Community sync client for OneDrive.

alternatives.name: OneDrive in a browser
alternatives.note: Access files on the web.

apps.notes: Microsoft has no OneDrive sync app for Linux. A community client or the web version works.

apps.name: iCloud

alternatives.name: iCloud in a browser
alternatives.note: View photos and files on icloud.com.

apps.notes: iCloud for Windows has no Linux version. Use icloud.com in a browser.

apps.name: Oracle VirtualBox
apps.notes: VirtualBox has an official Linux version for running other operating systems.

apps.name: VMware Workstation
apps.notes: VMware Workstation has an official Linux version for virtual machines.

apps.name: Wireshark
apps.notes: Wireshark has an official Linux version for network capture.

apps.name: Nmap
apps.notes: Nmap has an official Linux version for network scanning.

apps.name: Npcap

alternatives.name: libpcap (built in)
alternatives.note: Packet-capture library that Linux tools such as Wireshark already use.

apps.notes: Npcap is a Windows packet-capture driver. Linux has libpcap built in, so nothing needs installing.

apps.name: Beyond Compare
apps.notes: Beyond Compare has official Linux builds (.deb/.rpm); your licence key works there too. Meld is a free alternative.

apps.name: WinMerge

alternatives.name: Meld
alternatives.note: Visual file and folder comparison tool.

apps.notes: WinMerge is Windows-only. Meld offers the same side-by-side comparison.

apps.name: Tesseract OCR
apps.notes: Tesseract has Linux packages and works the same way on the command line.

apps.name: yt-dlp
apps.notes: yt-dlp is cross-platform and has Linux packages; commands are the same.

apps.name: FFmpeg
apps.notes: FFmpeg is built for Linux and most command-line scripts work unchanged.

apps.name: LM Studio
apps.notes: LM Studio has an official Linux version for running local AI models.

apps.name: Ollama
apps.notes: Ollama has an official Linux version for running local AI models.

apps.name: smartmontools
apps.notes: smartmontools is built for Linux and reports disk health.

apps.name: Technitium MAC Address Changer

alternatives.name: macchanger
alternatives.note: Command-line MAC address changer.

alternatives.name: NetworkManager settings
alternatives.note: Set a cloned MAC address per connection in network settings.

apps.notes: Technitium is Windows-only. Linux network settings can set a custom MAC address directly.

apps.name: Malwarebytes

alternatives.name: ClamAV
alternatives.note: Free open-source scanner for files and mail.

apps.notes: Malwarebytes has no consumer Linux app. Linux malware is far rarer; ClamAV covers on-demand scans.

apps.name: Norton

alternatives.name: ClamAV
alternatives.note: Free on-demand scanner.

apps.notes: Norton has no Linux consumer app. Most Linux systems do not need a separate antivirus.

apps.name: McAfee

alternatives.name: ClamAV
alternatives.note: Free on-demand scanner.

apps.notes: McAfee has no Linux consumer app. Most Linux systems do not need a separate antivirus.

apps.name: Avast

alternatives.name: ClamAV
alternatives.note: Free on-demand scanner.

apps.notes: Avast has no Linux consumer app. Most Linux systems do not need a separate antivirus.

apps.name: AVG

alternatives.name: ClamAV
alternatives.note: Free on-demand scanner.

apps.notes: AVG has no Linux consumer app. Most Linux systems do not need a separate antivirus.

apps.name: Bitdefender

alternatives.name: ClamAV
alternatives.note: Free on-demand scanner.

apps.notes: Bitdefender has no consumer Linux app. Most Linux systems do not need a separate antivirus.

apps.name: Kaspersky

alternatives.name: ClamAV
alternatives.note: Free on-demand scanner.

apps.notes: Kaspersky has no consumer Linux app. Most Linux systems do not need a separate antivirus.

apps.name: ESET

alternatives.name: ClamAV
alternatives.note: Free on-demand scanner.

apps.notes: ESET has no consumer Linux app. Most Linux systems do not need a separate antivirus.

apps.name: Windows Defender

alternatives.name: ClamAV
alternatives.note: Optional on-demand scanner.

apps.notes: Defender is Windows-only. Linux does not need it; ClamAV is available if you want a scanner.

apps.name: NordVPN
apps.notes: NordVPN has an official Linux app. Log in with the same account.

apps.name: ExpressVPN
apps.notes: ExpressVPN has an official Linux app for the same account.

apps.name: Proton VPN
apps.notes: Proton VPN has an official Linux app.

apps.name: Mullvad VPN
apps.notes: Mullvad has an official Linux app with the same account.

apps.name: Surfshark
apps.notes: Surfshark has an official Linux app.

apps.name: Private Internet Access
apps.notes: Private Internet Access has an official Linux app.

apps.name: Eddie
apps.notes: Eddie is the official AirVPN client and has a Linux version.

apps.name: WireGuard
apps.notes: WireGuard is built into recent Linux kernels; the tools install with one command.

apps.name: OpenVPN
apps.notes: OpenVPN has an official Linux version and supports the same server configs.

apps.name: Logitech G HUB

alternatives.name: Solaar
alternatives.note: Manages Logitech receivers and many mice and keyboards.

apps.notes: G HUB has no Linux version. Solaar covers most Logitech devices; RGB lighting may need OpenRGB.

apps.name: Razer Synapse

alternatives.name: Polychromatic
alternatives.note: Controls Razer devices through OpenRazer.

apps.notes: Razer Synapse has no Linux version. Polychromatic with OpenRazer covers lighting and DPI for many devices.

apps.name: Corsair iCUE

alternatives.name: OpenRGB
alternatives.note: Controls RGB on many brands, including Corsair.

alternatives.name: ckb-next
alternatives.note: Controls Corsair keyboards and mice.

apps.notes: iCUE has no Linux version. OpenRGB or ckb-next covers most Corsair lighting.

apps.name: SignalRGB

alternatives.name: OpenRGB
alternatives.note: Open-source RGB controller for many brands.

apps.notes: SignalRGB has no Linux version. OpenRGB covers most device lighting.

apps.name: NZXT CAM

alternatives.name: liquidctl
alternatives.note: Controls NZXT coolers, fans and LED controllers from the command line.

apps.notes: NZXT CAM has no Linux version. liquidctl covers most NZXT cooling hardware.

apps.name: L-Connect 3

alternatives.name: liquidctl
alternatives.note: Controls some Lian Li fan controllers; check device support.

apps.notes: L-Connect has no Linux version. liquidctl covers some Lian Li devices.

apps.name: ASUS Armoury Crate

alternatives.name: asusctl
alternatives.note: Controls ASUS laptop profiles and keyboard lighting.

alternatives.name: OpenRGB
alternatives.note: Controls RGB on many ASUS boards.

apps.notes: Armoury Crate has no Linux version. asusctl and OpenRGB cover most ASUS features.

apps.name: MSI Center

alternatives.name: OpenRGB
alternatives.note: Controls RGB on many MSI boards.

apps.notes: MSI Center has no Linux version. OpenRGB covers RGB; fan curves are set in the BIOS.

apps.name: AMD Software: Adrenalin Edition

alternatives.name: LACT
alternatives.note: Fan curves and GPU settings for AMD cards.

apps.notes: Adrenalin is Windows-only. Linux uses the built-in AMD graphics driver, and LACT adds tuning.

apps.name: AMD Ryzen Master

alternatives.name: lm-sensors
alternatives.note: Shows CPU temperatures and clocks on Linux.

apps.notes: Ryzen Master is Windows-only. Linux monitoring tools show the same temperatures and clocks.

apps.name: NVIDIA App

alternatives.name: NVIDIA driver with nvidia-settings
alternatives.note: Official Linux driver with its own settings tool.

apps.notes: The NVIDIA App and GeForce Experience are Windows-only. The Linux NVIDIA driver includes nvidia-settings for the same controls.

apps.name: Intel Driver & Support Assistant

alternatives.name: Built-in Linux drivers
alternatives.note: Intel graphics and chipset support is in the kernel and Mesa.

apps.notes: Intel's assistant is Windows-only. Linux uses built-in Intel drivers and updates through the package manager.

apps.name: Samsung Magician

alternatives.name: smartmontools
alternatives.note: Reads Samsung SSD health data.

apps.notes: Samsung Magician is Windows-only. smartmontools reports drive health on Linux.

apps.name: Meta Horizon Link

alternatives.name: ALVR
alternatives.note: Community tool that streams SteamVR games to a Quest.

apps.notes: Meta's Quest Link app has no Linux version. ALVR is a community option for PC VR on Linux.

apps.name: Voicemod

alternatives.name: EasyEffects
alternatives.note: Real-time voice and audio effects on Linux.

apps.notes: Voicemod has no Linux version. EasyEffects covers basic voice effects.

apps.name: Medal

alternatives.name: OBS Studio
alternatives.note: Records and replays gameplay.

apps.notes: Medal has no Linux version. OBS Studio records clips with replay buffer.

apps.name: VRChat
apps.notes: VRChat does not officially support Linux. Some users run it through Proton, but its anti-cheat can block it.

apps.name: AMD HIP SDK
apps.notes: HIP comes from AMD's ROCm, which is Linux-first; install ROCm from your distro or AMD's repository.

apps.name: .NET SDK
apps.notes: The .NET SDK has official Linux builds; package names include the version number.

apps.name: Deadlock Mod Manager
apps.notes: Community tool; Linux support not checked.
